source.notes: Scanned school paper with no text layer (only the icseboard.org watermark); OCR corrected against the page images. No school name is printed. Printed header: Grade- VIII, Time: 2 Hours, ASSESSMENT- II, CHEMISTRY, M.M. 80. No year is printed on the paper; examYear 2024 is taken from the file name (...-290224-2024) and the icseboard.org folder. Section A (40 marks) is compulsory; its seven groups (I-VII) print only a group total ([10], then [5] each), so each group is kept as one entry with that total (never split). Section B (40 marks) has seven questions of 8 marks each (sub-parts printed [3]/[5]) of which any five are to be attempted, so the listed marks add up to 96, not 80. Chemical subscripts are printed as subscripts on the scan and are written as Unicode subscripts; arrows as →. The paper's own wording and spellings (e.g. 'carbocation', 'tongs', 'u sed', 'powered charcoal', 'van der waals's') are kept. The Whatsapp advertisement on page 3 and the icseboard.org watermark are ignored. No answer key is printed.

questions.text:
Tick the correct answer:
1. Which of the following is not an amorphous form of carbon?
(a) coal (b) diamond (c) charcoal (d) lamp black
2. The process by which food is oxidised :
(a) photosynthesis (b) carbocation (c) respiration (d) tongs
3. Latent heat of vaporisation is :
(a) 2257 J/g (b) 2268 J/g (c) 226 J/g (d) 126 J/g
4. The metals which form ionic hydrides are :
(a) Li, Na, Zn (b) Li, Na, Ca (c) Na, Cu, Al (d) Zn, Mg, Al
5. When crystals of copper carbonate, which are green in colour, are heated strongly then it forms a :
(a) black compound of CuO (b) white compound of CuO (c) green compound of CuO (d) reaction does not take place
6. Allotropy is shown by :
(a) hydrogen (b) carbon (c) both (a) and (b) (d) none of these
7. Which acid is present in vinegar?
(a) acetic acid (b) boric acid (c) carbonic acid (d) ferric acid
8. Sacrificial protection is the coating of any substance with :
(a) nickel (b) zinc (c) manganese (d) copper
9. The metals which can be u sed for producing hydrogen gas by reacting them with steam are:
(a) Mg, Cd, Sn (b) Mg, Zn, Na (c) Mg, Zn, Fe (d) Zn, Sn, Cu
10. The reaction between lead nitrate and potassium iodide is an example of :
(a) double displacement reaction (b) single displacement reaction (c) decomposition reaction (d) neutralisation reaction
